nasal-breathing-cardio-warm-up.name: Nasal Breathing Cardio Warm Up
notes: If you're pain free, you can use a fast walk/jog as your warmup. Start slow and gradually ramp it up to a jogging pace. However, if you haven't been running consistently or you have pain when running, then you can use a fast walk OR a stationary bike, elliptical or any other low impact cardio machine.

split-stance-loaded-hip-rotations.name: Split Stance Loaded Hip Rotations
notes: -Use a light dumbbell or any form of additional weight 5-15 lbs is plenty of weight. -Hold onto a med ball or bench with the off hand for some added stability. -Complete the reps with right leg forward and right hand, THEN right leg forward left hand, THEN left leg forward left hand, THEN left leg forward right hand. That completes 1 set. -For example, if it says 8 reps that means RIGHT LEG forward with band around right thigh-- do 8 reps right hand THEN 8 reps left hand. Then switch the band to the left leg, put your left leg forward and complete 8 reps left hand then 8 reps right hand. A total of 32 repetitions per set.

hip-hinge-ankle-rocker.name: Hip Hinge Ankle Rocker
notes: Rest 30 to 45 seconds. 1 set = completion of recommended reps to each side.

half-kneeling-hip-flexor-stretch-paulfab.name: Half Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
notes: 1 set = completing recommended reps to both sides. If you don't have enough flexibility to grab your foot, you can use the alternate exercise as a regression for 5 reps (breaths). Click "alternate exercise" to view.

loaded-lateral-line-stretch.name: Loaded Lateral Line Stretch
notes: If you don't have the band, this stretch is still effective without it.

hip-mobility-er-ir-skips.name: Hip Mobility ER/IR Skips
notes: -Rest 30 seconds in-between sets. -Skip backwards with high knees and external hip rotation for 10 yards, then come forward with internal rotation skips for 10 yards. Continue repeating this cycle for the total recommended set time.

metronome-dot-drill.name: Metronome Dot Drill
notes: If you're advanced and pain free you can go straight to level 5 (150 beats per minute) Level 1 = 110 bpm Level 2 = 120 bpm Level 3 = 130 bpm Level 4 = 140 bpm Level 5 = 150 bpm If this is too difficult or causes pain, you can regress back to a 2 leg metronome jump. Click "alternate exercise" to view.

deep-knee-bend-extensive-jumps.name: Deep Knee Bend Extensive Jumps
notes: If this is too difficult or causes pain/discomfort, revert back to the extensive knee dominant plyo progression and begin at level 1. Click "alternate exercise" to view.

single-leg-full-range-step-downs-or-leg-.name: Single Leg Full Range Step Downs or Leg Press
notes: If you choose to go straight into the split stance variation, but you struggle to achieve full range of motion you have 2 options: 1) Shorten the depth as I demonstrated at 7:02 mark in the video. Or 2) you can add a heel wedge or 5 lb plate under the heel, which helps most people achieve a deeper range of motion. Instead of strength training at 100% of your max range, we want to go 80-90% of that maximum range and build strength there. Never FORCE a deeper range of motion. Work with the range you can comfortably achieve, and as you build strength near those natural end ranges you will probably free up deeper ranges. For people who struggle with range in the split squats, the leg press with a low foot position as seen in the video is GREAT for training the knee through a larger range of motion. The leg press also has more loading potential, so if your goal is pure lower body strength, it's a great option. It's also ok to do 2 sets of the leg press, then 2 sets of the split squat.

kickstand-rdl-paulfabritz.name: Kickstand RDL
notes: -Stand with light dumbbells in each hand. -If you master the dumbbell stage and run out of dumbbells in your gym, advanced lifters may use a trap bar if it’s available. -If you run out of dumbbells and you don’t have a trap bar available, simply slow down your reps to add time under tension to make it more difficult. -Use a range of motion that allows you to feel a moderate stretch in the hamstrings at the bottom. Caution- this exercise may not feel like a huge burn, but it does cause a fair amount of soreness the following day if you increase difficulty too early.

razor-curl-progressions.name: Razor Curl Progressions
notes: Rest 45-60 seconds before going back into the back leg lunge. Level 1 = Shortened range of motion Level 2 = Full range of motion, push back up with hands (no concentric portion) Level 3 = Full range + concentric

cable-rotation-hip-flexor-drive.name: Cable Rotation Hip Flexor Drive
notes: If this variation is too advanced or you don't have the balance/stability to do this option, click "alternate exercise" to view the easier variation. Remember, either variation could be done with just a band if you don't have the cable machine. 1 set = recommended reps on both legs

lateral-ankle-slant-board-cooker.name: Lateral Ankle Slant Board Cooker
notes: The small calf raise is used to pre fatigue the muscles. Once you reach about an 8/10 burn, THEN begin the rotations for the recommended reps.

hip-flexor-length-under-load.name: Hip Flexor Length Under Load
notes: Level 1 = knee stays on floor, hold onto something for assistance Level 2 = knee comes off floor (holding in long split squat position), hold onto something for assistance. Find a depth that feels like a stretch but doesn't cause pain or excessive discomfort Level 3 = hold in long split squat, begin to oscillate (pulse) up and down just a few inches. We're still holding onto something for assistance. Level 4 = same position as level 3, small up and down pulse but NO hand assistance. Level 5 = lightly weighted. Grab a dumbbell or kettlebell and hold it in your hands between your legs (under your hips). Pulse up and down a few inches. Level 6 = same as level 5, except we use bumper plates or small boxes to stand on in order to get deeper range of motion. Level 7 = same as level 6, except we add a small turn towards the front leg to stretch the rotational fibers in the back hip flexor. Regression if these cause pain/discomfort--Click "alternate exercise" to view.

lateral-lunge-length-under-load.name: Lateral Lunge Length Under Load
notes: Level 1 = feet on floor Level 2 = non loaded leg elevated on bumper plate or small step 3-6 inches Level 3 = non loaded leg elevated on box, bench or chair around mid shin to knee height Level 4 = non loaded leg elevated on box, bench or chair around mid shin to knee height AND the loaded leg elevated on bumper plate or small step 3-6 inches. If these variations are too difficult or cause pain/excess discomfort, use this regression instead. Click "alternate exercise" to view.

optional-pigeon-length-under-load.name: Optional Pigeon Length Under Load
notes: -Work through these progressions slowly. Level 3 and 4 can be very difficult for many athletes. Level 1 = lying on your back, figure 4 stretch. Level 2 = pigeon stretch with extended back leg, heavy on hands, slowly lower chest towards knee. Level 3 = same position, remove hands from floor and keep hands straight out to your side. Lower yourself slowly until chest reaches your knee, slowly raise back up. Level 4 = hands to side, lift out and bring back leg around to reach tall kneeling position. Slowly reverse the movement and lower back to starting position. -Only move onto the next level when you’ve mastered the form of the previous variation and you feel like you need a new challenge

shoulder-mobility-pullovers.name: Shoulder Mobility Pullovers
notes: -Perform this exercise with a light weight around 5-10 lbs and lie down on a bench or on the floor on your back. -Make sure you keep contact between your lower back and the bench on this exercise. This, along with the feet elevated on the bench will train your pelvis to avoid excessive anterior tilt, which allows for better rib cage and shoulder mechanics.

bear-crawl-movement.name: Bear Crawl (Movement)
notes: 4 steps forward (2 with each leg), the 4 steps backwards completes 1 repetition. If this variation is too difficult or causes pain, you can click the "alternative exercise" to try an All Four Alternating Belly Lift. *Rotational concepts discussed in the video are inspired by Weck Method.

barbell-rollout-two-variations.name: Barbell Rollout: Two Variations
notes: Level 1 = inch worm (feet moving, arms still) Level 2 = barbell or ab wheel or stability ball rollout

split-stance-cable-press-paulfabritz.name: Split Stance Cable Press
notes: If this exercise form is too difficult for you to master or you don't have access to the cable machine you can use a dumbbell bench press instead. Click "alternate exercise" to view.

split-stance-lat-pull-down.name: Split Stance Lat Pull Down
notes: If you don't have access to a cable machine you can use a regular lat pulldown machine instead. If you don't have access to a lat pulldown you can do assisted pullups.

landmine-or-dumbbell-dip-press.name: Landmine or Dumbbell Dip Press
notes: If you have a hard time with overhead pressing variations due to shoulder mobility, and you don't have access to a landmine set up then you can regress to a DB incline bench press. Click "alternate exercise" to view. 1 set = completion of reps on both sides

landmine-or-dumbbell-rotational-row.name: Landmine or Dumbbell Rotational Row
notes: If these variations are too difficult or cause pain, you can try an inverted row instead. Click "alternate exercise" to view. 1 set = completion of reps on both sides

towel-curl-paulfabritz.name: Towel Curl
notes: If you don't have the towel you can use a rope extension for the cable machine. Or you can use a dumbbell incline curl if you do not have access to a cable machine. Click "alternate exercise" to view.

towel-tricep-extension.name: Towel Tricep Extension
notes: If you don't have the towel, you can use a regular rope cable extension as seen in this video. Click "alternate exercise" to view.

rock-back-breathing.name: Rock Back Breathing
notes: Reps are counting in breaths

toe-motor-control.name: Toe Motor Control
notes: Curl the toes, hold for 2 seconds, then lift the toes as high as you can towards your head, hold for 2 seconds, then spread the toes as wide as possible, hold 2 seconds, then repeat the cycle. Perform as many reps as the total set time will allow for.

wall-side-posture-reach.name: Wall Side Posture Reach
notes: *Exercise inspired by ELDOA Technique

cat-camel-paulfabritz.name: Cat Camel
notes: 1 rep = down (cat) and up (camel).

griffith-wall-rotations.name: Griffith Wall Rotations
notes: 1 set = completing recommended reps on both sides *Exercise inspired by Vernon Griffith

slant-board-isometric-progressions.name: Slant Board Isometric Progressions
notes: Elevate your heel on a weighted plate, small wedge or book if you don’t have a slant board Level 1 = hand assistance for additional support Level 2 = bodyweight only Level 3 = hold a backpack or light dumbbells for additional weight Always start with a VERY small knee bend. Once you prove you can complete the set pain free you may begin to bend the knee up to 60-80 degrees. Only progress to the next level if you’re pain free and you are no longer getting an 8/10 burn in the quads by the end of the set If the slant board iso is too difficult or causes pain, click "alternative exercise" to use the 60 degree iso hold as a regression. The same reps and sets apply to the regression.

2-leg-hamstring-iso.name: 2 Leg Hamstring Iso
notes: -Lay on your back and bend your knees slightly. -Drive your heels into the ground to lift your hips off the floor until you achieve full hip extension. Hold in this position for the recommended set time. -You should feel the burn in your hamstrings, not your lower back. If you feel it in your lower back you are likely hyperextending the spine instead of extending the hips. -If you cannot achieve an 8/10 burn in the hamstrings with just your bodyweight, you can move to level 2 by adding weight on top of the hips. -Find a weight that allows you to achieve an 8/10 burn with no pain in the knees and back

resisted-ankle-circles.name: Resisted Ankle Circles
notes: -Use a PJF fabric mini band and tie it around a light weight. The weight must be very light to start— 2.5 to 5 lbs is ideal. -Perform the recommended reps in a clockwise direction, then perform the reps in a counter clockwise direction. Then switch legs to complete the set. -Only go up in weight if you can no longer achieve an 8/10 burn in the shin/ankle muscles. As always, scale back or skip the exercise if you experience pain in the ankles.

hip-flexor-quad-bridge.name: Hip Flexor/Quad Bridge
notes: Level 1 = elbows resting on couch, bench or chair. Level 2 = elbows off, now upper back is resting on couch, bench or chair. Level 3 = remove couch, bench or chair. Extend arms and use hands to support you on the floor. Level 4 = use elbows/forearms to support you on the floor. Some people experience knee pain with these variations. If level 1 knee pain or any other joint pain, use this regression instead-- Click "alternate exercise" to view.

front-chain-stretch-w-reach-and-turn.name: Front Chain Stretch w/ Reach and Turn

optional-foam-roll-circuit.name: Optional Foam Roll Circuit
notes: 25-45 seconds each -Glutes, hamstrings, calves, quads/hip flexors, lacrosse or golf ball on bottom of feet.

supine-alternating-cross-connect-paulfab.name: Supine Cross Connect
notes: reps = breaths (inhale through the nose, long exhale out the mouth).

rolling-arm-bar-w-screwdriver-rotation.name: Rolling Arm Bar w/ Screwdriver Rotation
notes: This drill works miracles for building hip internal rotation mobility, but the details can be a bit tricky. It’s ok if you don’t get it down day 1. Follow the directions in the video but I want you to especially think about the following tips when you perform the exercise. The leg that is down on the ground must be actively pushed into the floor throughout the entire exercise. Don’t lose pressure in that leg or you won’t get the hip mobility benefits. Breath in through the nose as you roll over, and out through the mouth when you roll back to the starting position. Keep the knee that is down fully locked out and the foot dorsiflexed (toes pulled up towards your head). Make sure the additional weight is light, between 10 and 20 lbs.

walking-sprinters-mobility.name: Walking Sprinters Mobility
notes: 1 set = completion of recommended reps on each leg. *Exercise idea inspired by compound performance

extensive-locomotion-cariocas.name: Extensive Locomotion Cariocas
notes: As always, if this exercise cause pain, skip it and move on to the next exercise. Level 1 = foot cycles over ANKLE level (low) Level 2 = foot cycles over MID SHIN level (medium) Level 3 = foot cycles over KNEE level (High) Level 4 = weighted vest or medicine ball + KNEE level cycle (High)

backwards-extensive-locomotive-skips.name: Backwards Extensive Locomotive Skips
notes: Level 1 = backwards skips foot coming over ANKLE Level 2 = backwards skips foot coming over MID SHIN Level 3 = backwards skips foot coming over KNEE Level 4 = WEIGHTED vest or dumbbells + backwards skips foot coming over KNEE

extensive-locomotive-skips.name: Extensive Locomotive Skips
notes: As always, if this exercise cause pain, skip it and move on to the next exercise. Level 1 = foot cycles over ANKLE level (low) Level 2 = foot cycles over MID SHIN level (medium) Level 3 = foot cycles at KNEE level (High) Level 4 = weighted vest or medicine ball + KNEE level cycle (High)

wide-stance-length-under-load.name: Wide Stance Length Under Load
notes: If this exercise causes discomfort or pain, or simply makes you feel even more tight after you finish you may not need additional hamstring stretching and you can skip this exercise.

long-length-hamstring-rapid-loading.name: Long Length Hamstring Rapid Loading
notes: -Level 1 = Skip with toe reaching mid shin level -Level 2 = Straight leg bound with toe reaching shin level -Level 3 = Straight leg bound pushing for bigger distance

scalable-impact-durability.name: Scalable Impact Durability
notes: Use 4-6 inch box, step or bumper plate. Level 1= lift front foot, push into the box just hard enough to step up onto the box (not a jump yet). Level 2= start in same position, now strike the box hard. Still not jumping. Level 3 = now start with leg high (thigh should be parallel to the floor in starting position). Strike the box hard. Still not a jump. Level 4 = start in same position as level 3, strike the box hard and jump 20-40% of maximal jump height. Level 5 = start in same position as level 3 and 4, strike the box hard and jump as high as possible (100% max jump height)

metronome-decels.name: Metronome Decels
notes: If the side to side movement is too difficult for you or causes pain, you can try regressing to a split stance switch and stick. Click "alternate exercise" to view.

rapid-forward-decels.name: Rapid Forward Decels
notes: Level 1- rapid switches. Both feet hit the floor at the same time. Level 2- start in split stance, stride back leg forward, rapidly decelerate and push back to starting position. Level 3- same exercise as level 2, except now we add dumbbells in our hands or a weighted vest.

ffe-rotational-split-squat.name: FFE Rotational Split Squat
notes: 1 set = both sides. If this exercise causes pain or it's too difficult for you, use the RFE regression instead and perform 2-3 sets of 25 seconds. Click to view "alternate exercise".

copenhagen-side-plank-paulfabritz.name: Copenhagen Side Plank
notes: Level 1 = bodyweight Level 2= additional weight on top hip If level 1 is too difficult or causes any pain you can skip to the 1:30 mark of the video to see the regressions to make it easier. 1 set = completing both sides.

ankle-mobility-lift-off.name: Ankle Mobility Lift Off
notes: 1 rep = pickup toes, slide forward, set the toes down.

soleus-raise-paulfabritz.name: Soleus Raise
notes: If you have access to a seated calf raise machine (bent knee), this is our best option. If not, we can use the other option shown in the video on 1 leg.

rotational-rdl-length-under-load.name: Rotational RDL Length Under Load
notes: If this exercise causes discomfort or pain, you can skip it or try an unloaded post chain stretch as a regression. Click "alternate exercise" to view.

curved-tempo-runs.name: Curved Tempo Runs
notes: 1 set = down 30 yards AND back 30 yards, THEN take your rest period before your next set. Use 3 cones spaced 10 yards apart. If you are 100% injury free and have been sprinting consistently, you can skip to 80-90% max speed in week 1. Then in week 2 ramp it up to 90-100%. But if you have not been sprinting consistently and/or you're coming back from an injury you may want to start at 50% speed week 1, 60-70% week 2, 70-90% week 3 and 90-100% week 4. Only progress intensities if you're pain free.

heels-elevated-narrow-squat.name: Heels Elevated Narrow Squat
notes: Level 1 = heel elevated + assistance Level 2 = heel elevated, bodyweight Level 3 = heel elevated + dumbbell or kettlebell goblet position Level 4 = heel elevated + barbell (front OR back squat position), whatever you're more comfortable with. If level 1 causes pain, you can use less range of motion. If it still causes pain then regress back to isometrics for 2-3 sets of 45 second holds. Click "alternate exercise" to view.

eccentric-nordic-hamstring-curl-paulfabr.name: Eccentric Nordic Hamstring Curl
notes: -Level 1 = perform the eccentric (lowering) but use your hands to push back up. Don’t perform the upward phase. -Level 2 = perform the eccentric and the concentric but use a push off with the hands to help yourself get up. -Level 3 = add weight on the way down, set the weight down and push off with your hands to get back up.

hip-shift-squat.name: Hip Shift Squat
notes: If this position is too difficult for you to master, you can use this regression-- Click "alternate exercise" to view".

staggered-stance-rdl-w-same-side-load.name: Staggered Stance RDL w/ Same Side Load

ballistic-wall-side-hip-extension.name: Ballistic Wall Side Hip Extension
notes: If you do not feel ready for the dynamic (fast) variation of this exercise. You can start slow and controlled. Click to view the "alternative exercise" for be another beginner level alternative

one-leg-rdl-rotation-w-toes-off.name: One Leg RDL Rotation w/ Toes Off
notes: If this is too difficult unassisted, you can try this regression instead. Click "alternate exercise" to view.

single-leg-motor-control-squat-calf-rais.name: Single Leg Motor Control Squat/Calf Raise

crossover-step-adductor-stretch.name: Crossover Step Adductor Stretch
notes: 1 rep = over and back If this is too advanced or causes pain, you can try the static adductor stretch progressions instead. Click "alternate exercise" to view.

short-accel-decel-progressions.name: Short Accel/Decel Progressions
notes: Level 1= 5 yard acceleration + 5 yards of room to decelerate. Level 2= 5 yard acceleration + only 2 yards of room to decelerate. 1 set = completion of recommended reps to one side , then completion of recommended reps to the other side.

eccentric-depth-drop-progressions.name: Altitude Drop Progressions
notes: -If you are able to jump maximally pain free, you can skip straight to expert level on this drill. However, if jumping and landing still causes pain in your joints you may want to start at beginner/intermediate level and prove to yourself you can do this drill pain free. -Beginner Level = Start at 50% of your standing vertical jump height, progress by 2 inches per week. -Intermediate Level = Start at 50% of your standing vertical jump height, progress by 2 inches per week. -Expert = Start with a box height of your standing vertical jump height. Progress box height by 4 inches per week.

90-90-knee-roll.name: 90/90 Knee Roll
notes: Don't worry about counting breaths here. You may simply set your timer and get those hips moving! *Exercise inspired by Postural Restoration Institute and David Grey

all-four-prone-hip-shift-drill.name: All Four Prone Hip Shift Drill
notes: 1 rep = over and back. If this drill is too difficult you can use a supine 90/90 knee roll as a regression, just click to view the "alternative exercise".

cable-rotation-rib-dissociation.name: Cable Rotation/Rib Dissociation
notes: -If you don’t have access to a cable, use a band for this exercise. -You should feel a burn in the obliques (side abs), but we shouldn’t be working with too heavy of a weight. -This exercise should feel rhythmic and fluid. -Make sure your pelvis doesn’t rotate along with your ribs/spine. Pelvis has to stay locked in place in order to get the dissociation in the ribs/spine.

eyes-closed-diagonal-steps.name: Eyes Closed Diagonal Steps
notes: Level 1 = eyes closed SMALL steps Level 2 = eyes closed MEDIUM sized steps Level 3 = eyes closed BIG steps (small bound) If you are high risk for falls, have poor balance or this exercise causes pain, skip this exercise and try a stationary regression. Click to view "alternate exercise". Don't worry about counting reps, simply set your timer and get going!

hip-loaded-diagonal-jumps.name: Hip Loaded Diagonal Jumps
notes: Level 1 = bodyweight. Start with small side to side jumps and gradually increase distance. Level 2 = lightly loaded. 5-10 lb dumbbells. 1 repetition = over and back (left and right side)

mutli-direction-bounds.name: Mutli-direction Bounds
notes: If this is too difficult for you, regress back to this Euro Step Balance drill. Click "alternate exercise" to view.

rdl-row-w-rotation.name: RDL Row w/ Rotation
notes: If this variation is too difficult or you don't have access to a cable machine you can use the 1 leg dumbbell RDL as a regression. Click "alternate exercise" to view.

one-leg-rdl-same-side-load.name: One Leg RDL Same Side Load

knee-step-overs.name: Knee Step Overs
notes: Level 1 = bodyweight with small range of motion and small step length. Gradually work to get more range of motion and longer step length. Level 2 = dumbbells in each hand 5-25 lbs to start. Level 3 = keep the same dumbbell weight and add a resistance band pulling you forward (or use a cable machine/belt around hips). 1 set = completion of recommended reps on each side

lateral-crossover-sled-drag-fatigue-coor.name: Lateral Crossover Sled Drag Fatigue/Coordination
notes: Perform the sled crossover drag (or band crossover as a substitution) for the recommended reps (measured in time) on BOTH sides. Then without taking a break, immediately begin the carioca to challenge coordination under fatigue. Remember, the carioca coordination drill is performed for HALF the reps (time) of the weighted drag. So if the recommended reps said 40 seconds, that means 40 seconds down with the weighted drag, switch sides, 40 seconds back. Then 20 seconds on the unloaded carioca. Then take your rest period before beginning your next set. If you don't have the sled, perform with a band (have a friend walk with you resisting you with the band). Or you can do a stationary cable or band crossover step, come back to starting position then repeat.

rfess-with-bilateral-load.name: RFESS Progessions
notes: If this exercise causes pain or discomfort, you can regress back to isometrics. Click "alternate exercise" to view.

dynamic-warm-up-2-paulfabritz.name: Dynamic Warm Up 2
notes: Skips 1x30 seconds Seal Jacks 1x30 seconds Post tilt hip bridge 1x10 reps T Spine side lying opener 1x7 reps each side 1/2 Kneel hip flexor stretch 1x10 each side Hamstring crossover touches 1x7 each side Knee hug lateral lunge 1x4 each side Hip flip forward 1x10 yards total Hip flip backwards 1x10 yards total

inverted-row-paulfabritz.name: Inverted Row
notes: Intensity:

band-resisted-bridge-march.name: Band Resisted Bridge March
notes: Perform Each Side

complex-landmine-or-db.name: Complex (Landmine or DB)
notes: Perform Each Side This exercise will be the same reps on ALL variations. For example, if it says 7 reps that means 7 split stance presses, 7 dip presses, 7 rdls.

tricep-push-down-iso-hold.name: Tricep Push Down Iso Hold (Optional)
notes: 1 rep= 5 second hold. So if it says 5 reps that means you do one rep (hold at bottom for 5 seconds), come back up, then repeat 5 times.

towel-inverted-curl.name: Towel Inverted Curl (Optional)
notes: Use a towel and wrap it around a pole or something stable that won’t fall over. If you don’t have something to anchor the towel to, simply loop the towel around your backpack and do curls with that instead Remember to squeeze the towel hard to get the grip strength benefits

static-stretch-23462eef-4989-4496-be91-a.name: Optional Static Stretch
notes: The post workout stretch is optional. If you don't have extra time it's ok to skip this, it won't make a big difference in terms of recovery. However, if you're someone that is very tight it can be beneficial. It's also ok to do this later at night or earlier in the morning if you don't have time to do it at the end of your workout.

wall-side-t-spine-opener.name: Wall Side T Spine Opener
notes: Perform Each Side

core-rotation-pallof-press.name: Core Rotation Pallof Press
notes: Perform Each Side

brettzel-stretch-or-brettzel-t-spin-open.name: Brettzel Stretch
notes: Perform Each Side

dumbbell-kickstand-clean-press.name: Dumbbell Kickstand Clean/Press
notes: Keep in mind, not everyone has the mobility to safely overhead press. If you can't comfortably get the dumbbells above the head without tipping forward or extending (arching) your back, then skip the press and just do the kickstand clean.

push-ups-paulfabritz.name: Push Ups
notes: We're aiming for as many reps as possible. However, do NOT come to technical failure. That means our form should never be compromised to achieve more repetitions. We want to stop about 1-2 reps short of failure.

sled-march-or-band-pull-through.name: Sled March or Band Pull Through
notes: If you're using the band option you'll do 10 repetitions -OR- go until you feel an 8/10 burn. Remember, if you choose the band pull through option you are doing 10 reps each leg. You are only going by yards if you choose the sled option.

kb-swing-box-jump-contrast.name: KB Swing + Box Jump Contrast
notes: Remember, if it says 10-5 that means 10 on the first exercise and 5 on the second exercise.

1-4-squats-or-1-4-leg-press.name: 1/4 Squats or 1/4 Leg Press
notes: Perform Each Side

90-90-hip-opener.name: 90/90 Hip Opener
notes: Perform Each Side

anti-rotations-abc.name: Anti Rotation ABC's
notes: 1 Repetition = A-J. If don't feel the burn by the time you get to J, then go heavier. If you are using the band option and you don't feel the burn by the time you get to J, then continue going through the alphabet until you feel an 8 or 9 out of 10 burn in the core.

dumbbell-lateral-raise-post-delt-row-dro.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise + Post Delt Row Drop Set

velocity-squat-penultimate-contrast.name: Velocity Squat + Penultimate Contrast
notes: We're doing 5 reps on the Velocity Squat, then 2 reps each side (4 total) on the penultimate. That completes 1 set. Rest and repeat for 4 total sets.

posterior-lateral-lunge.name: Posterior Lateral Lunge
notes: Perform Each Side

wall-side-t-spine-band-rotations.name: Wall Side T Spine Band Rotations

contrast-step-ups.name: Contrast Step Ups
notes: We're doing 4 reps on the weighted step up AND 4 reps on the bodyweight step-up jump. Perform Each Side

cat-cow.name: Cat Cow
notes: 1 rep = down (cat) and up (camel).

push-up-to-pike.name: Push-Up To Pike
notes: Push-up, then press the hips up and back into a pike (down dog). Back to plank, repeat.

b-stance-rdl.name: B-Stance RDL
notes: -Stand with light dumbbells in each hand. -If you master the dumbbell stage and run out of dumbbells in your gym, advanced lifters may use a trap bar if it’s available. -If you run out of dumbbells and you don’t have a trap bar available, simply slow down your reps to add time under tension to make it more difficult. -Use a range of motion that allows you to feel a moderate stretch in the hamstrings at the bottom. Caution- this exercise may not feel like a huge burn, but it does cause a fair amount of soreness the following day if you increase difficulty too early.

dayNotes.note: Time to get some BIG GAINS! Let's get to work!!
